resources.string: After you stop speaking, replaces Moonshine\'s punctuation (a period at every pause) with proper sentences, commas and capitals. Your words stay as they are.
Needs a punctuation model. Add one in Languages & Models → Punctuation Model.

Whisper adds its own punctuation, so the punctuation model isn\'t used while Whisper is your voice model. (Whisper is also the only voice model for languages other than English.) Switch your voice model to Moonshine to use it.
Skipped while Whisper is your voice model, since Whisper adds its own punctuation. This is for Moonshine.
After you stop speaking, reads the whole sentence and fixes words the voice model misheard. It never rephrases what you said, and everything stays on your phone.
Needs a Smart corrections model. Add one in Languages & Models → Smart Corrections.
Fixes misheard words using the whole sentence.
Little benefit with Whisper (your current voice model). It\'s meant for Moonshine.

Whisper is your current voice model. It already reads your whole dictation for context, so Smart corrections will change little and add a short wait after you stop speaking. Smart corrections are meant for Moonshine.
Choose what Smart corrections may change.
Turn on Smart corrections to use this.
Swaps a word for one that sounds the same when the sentence calls for it, like “bulls” → “bowls” or “in to” → “into”.
Spells names and words from your personal dictionary the way you do, and fixes stray capital letters.
Writes spoken numbers as digits, like “twenty five dollars” → “$25” or “three thirty pm” → “3:30 PM”.
How readily each correction changes what you said.
Each correction only changes your words when the sentence clearly reads better. Slide left if one changes words it should leave alone, or right if it misses changes you want.
Adds quotation marks when you repeat what someone said, but only when the sentence makes it clear. “He was like ten feet tall” stays as it is.
Say “laughing emoji” → 😂 or “heart emoji” → ❤️. When you\'re talking about an emoji, like “the heart emoji is my favorite”, the words stay.

Each emoji answers to its nicknames, Unicode name and keywords, in the plural, in any word order, and without “face” or “with”. A name that fits several emoji gives none. Search to see which names give an emoji, switch one off, or add your own.
Built-in names are off, so only your own names give this emoji.
No name of yours yet. Tap to add one.
Search a word or an emoji
Search to see which names give which emoji. Names you add or switch off are listed here.
Names you added or switched off
No emoji has that name. Add it as your own below.
“%1$s emoji” gives no emoji (it fits several, or is switched off). Add it as your own name to choose one.
Showing the first %1$d. Type more to narrow it down.
That name is already in your list.
Remove the names you added and switch every built-in name back on?

After someone and one of these phrases, like “she said” or “I was like”, the rest of the sentence becomes a quote, but only when it can only be something they said (a question, or a reply that starts with “um”, “oh” or “wow”). “He fired back with a shotgun” stays as it is. Switch a phrase off to stop using it.
That phrase is already in the list.
Delete the phrases you added and switch every built-in phrase back on?
%d built-in phrases. Turn this off and only the ones you add start a quote.
Removes “um”, “uh”, a “like” or “basically” between pauses, and words you said twice by accident. Fillers inside a quote are kept.
Say “new line”, “comma” or “scratch that” to format as you speak, with a short pause before or after. When the words are part of your sentence, like “a new line formed”, they stay as words.
When you change your mind mid-sentence, like “Tuesday, no wait, Wednesday”, keeps only the correction. Phrases like “I mean it” stay as they are.
No commands yet. Add one below.
That phrase is already in the list.
Undo your changes to this list
Replace your list with the built-in commands?

When you say one of these, the words just before it are replaced by the words after it, but only when the sentence shows you were correcting yourself. Switch a phrase off to stop using it. Phrases you add work best with a short pause before them.
That phrase is already in the list.
Delete the phrases you added and switch every built-in phrase back on?
%d built-in phrases. Turn this off and only the ones you add mark a correction.
These are removed from what you say, except where the sentence needs them, like inside a quote. Switch one off to always keep it. Fillers you add are only removed in the middle of a sentence.
You haven\'t added any filler words.
Reset to the built-in filler words
Delete the filler words you added and switch every built-in one back on?
%d built-in filler words. Turn this off and only the ones you add are removed.
Off for now. Turn on the switch above to use these too.
Live text, auto-stop and speed settings for live voice typing
These settings only apply when a Moonshine model is your English voice input model (Languages & Models).
Words appear as you speak. Turn this off and each phrase appears when you pause, which uses less battery but takes a moment longer when you finish.
How often the words on screen catch up with your speech. Faster feels more live but uses more battery.
When you stop talking for this long, voice typing finishes and types your words, as if you tapped to finish. When it\'s off, it keeps listening until you tap. Background noise can keep it listening.
How live voice typing runs on your phone. Standard is usually fastest, and you can turn on Show timing info to compare. If a mode doesn\'t work on your phone, Standard is used instead.
How many processor cores live voice typing uses. Auto picks your phone\'s fast cores (more isn\'t always faster).
After live voice typing, shows how long you spoke and how long it took to process.
Types your words after you finish speaking. Works in many languages.
Live, so words appear as you speak, with no time limit. English only. %1$s
For live voice typing in English, import a Moonshine model package (.zip).
A Whisper model file (.bin) or a Moonshine model package (.zip)
Delete %1$s? You\'ll need to import it again to use it.

After you stop speaking, the punctuation model takes out Moonshine\'s punctuation and punctuates what you said again, with real sentences, commas and capital letters. Moonshine\'s question marks and exclamation marks are kept, because it heard your tone of voice. Your words stay as they are. The model you choose is used for every language it supports.
Keep punctuation as the voice model wrote it
Periods, commas, question marks, capital letters and sentence breaks. %1$s
Periods, commas and question marks in many languages. %1$s
No punctuation model for this language is installed yet.

After you stop speaking, Smart corrections reads the whole sentence with a small language model and fixes words the voice model misheard. It can also write numbers as digits, follow voice commands like “new line”, remove filler words, fix self-corrections, add quotation marks and type emoji by name. It never rephrases what you said, works entirely offline and adds up to about two seconds. Choose what it may change in Voice Input → Smart corrections.
Keep the words as the voice model wrote them
Fixes misheard words, names and more using the whole sentence. %1$s
No Smart corrections model for this language is installed yet.
Smart corrections needs a newer processor (ARMv8.2 or later), so it can\'t run on this phone.
